svg.text: The first minute of life: air, warmth, and nothing clever
Almost every baby who needs help needs only ventilation
At birth, in order, within sixty seconds
Dry the baby thoroughly and remove the wet cloth — drying is itself the stimulation
Keep warm: cap on, skin to skin if breathing, under a warmer if not
Position the head neutral, not tipped back like an adult
If not breathing after drying and rubbing the back: start bag and mask, 40–60 breaths a minute
What wastes the golden minute
Routine suction of a baby who is breathing
Holding the baby up by the ankles
Slapping, shaking, or squeezing the chest
Waiting for the Apgar score at one minute
Apgar records what happened; it does not decide
whether to resuscitate
If the chest is not rising
Reapply the mask — the seal is the usual fault
Reposition the head to neutral
Suction only now, if secretions are blocking
Open the mouth slightly, squeeze a little harder
Ventilation that moves no air is not ventilation
Cold kills quietly
A wet newborn loses heat within minutes,
even in a warm Ghanaian labour ward.
Hypothermia worsens breathing, lowers
glucose and increases death. Dry and cover.
If the baby is breathing well
Skin to skin on the mother’s chest, covered
Delay cord clamping at least one minute
Breastfeed within the first hour
Weighing and bathing can wait
